## Additional defect 3 — the same clock bug can destroy EPS's OWN parked pods

The `created_at` staleness clock (line 357) is not only a teammate hazard. For an
EPS-owned pod the ownership gate passes trivially (signal 1), so ANY `pod-<N>`
that is merely STOPPED — `pod.py stop`, the watcher's reversible auto-stop, a park
— is terminate-eligible at the next 09:37 run if it was CREATED >24h ago, with no
grace period at all. The only thing standing between a parked EPS pod and volume
destruction is the `keep-running` tag.

Live example at filing time: `pod-1739` (`yib7yjxjvmx6iz`) is EXITED and appears in
today's audit under `kept-exited` solely because task #1739 carries `keep-running`.
Remove that tag and the next run destroys the volume.

This mechanizes the hazard `.claude/rules/pod-config.md` already warns about
("a STOPPED volume is NOT durable", #1112) — the audit turns a reversible park into
an irreversible delete within <24h. The fix (measure from EXIT, not creation) closes
the teammate case and this one together, but the plan should state the EPS-side
case explicitly and test it.

## Additional defect 4 — zero alerting on an irreversible action

`pod_audit.py` has NO notification path (no telegram/push/alert call), and
`cron_pod_audit.sh` deliberately `exit 0`s even on rc=2 with the comment "we don't
want cron emails on every 'found and terminated stale pod' event". The only record
is `logs/pod_audit/YYYY-MM-DD.log`.

Every OTHER destructive fleet cron notifies: `vm_disk_guard.py`, `gcp_audit.py`, and
`autonomous_session_watch.py` all push. `pod_audit.py` is the sole destructive cron
that is silent — which is why 77 terminations across 14 days went unnoticed until a
teammate asked in chat.

Requirement: any auto-terminate must emit one push naming the pods destroyed. A
silent irreversible action on a SHARED account is the root reason this incident had
a 2-week detection lag.

## What is now in force

1. **RunPod hard interlock at the single choke point.**
   `runpod_api.terminate_pod` refuses unless authorized. Every RunPod
   destruction path routes through it — the daily stale-pod audit, `/issue`
   Step 8 teardown, both `backend_poll` wedge failovers (#770/#775), and the
   watcher's wedge arm. Gated at the choke point rather than per call site: a
   per-caller guard would have to be re-litigated for every future call site.

   Exactly TWO authorizations exist:
   - **User approval** — `pod.py terminate --issue N --yes --approve` (new
     flag), or `EPS_ALLOW_COMPUTE_KILL=1 <cmd>` (legacy alias
     `EPS_ALLOW_POD_TERMINATE=1` still honored). Env-based, per-invocation,
     never persisted; the crontab environment does not set it, which is what
     disarms every scheduled destructive path at once.
   - **Owner-driven verified teardown** — a thread-local in-process
     `backends.kill_approval.verified_teardown` grant that
     `pod_lifecycle.cmd_terminate` enters ONLY AFTER
     `_guard_upload_verification_before_terminate` passes. That guard IS the
     mechanical meaning of "everything is uploaded", so passing it authorizes
     exactly the teardown it just cleared. This implements the user's
     refinement: the agent driving a job may close its own pod.

   A cron / watcher / janitor / any background sweep holds NEITHER and is
   refused. A refusal fires one push deduped per (pod_id, UTC day) so an
   approval-blocked teardown surfaces instead of silently idle-billing.

2. **`cron_pod_audit.sh` DISABLED at the crontab** (the `37 9 * * *` entry that
   destroyed the 77 teammate pods). Backup of the prior crontab at
   `/tmp/crontab.bak.*`. Re-arming it is part of THIS task's completion and
   only after the regression tests land.

3. **`cron_gcp_audit.sh` forced report-only** — its crontab entry now carries
   `EPS_GCP_JANITOR_DRY_RUN=1`.

## Deliberate scope decisions (do not "fix" these without re-deciding)

- **GCP `render_delete_argv` is NOT code-gated.** Every caller is an owner
  teardown of an EPS-created instance, and GCP provisioning is disabled
  (#2028), so no new GCE instance can be created at all; gating it would block
  in-flight owner teardown and leak billing VMs for zero safety gain. The
  scheduled janitor — the only shuts-down-on-its-own actor on that lane — is
  contained at the cron (item 3). A one-line note to this effect is in the
  renderer docstring so a future reader does not "close the gap".
- **The watcher's reversible auto-STOP (`pod.py stop`) is NOT gated.** Stop is
  not a kill (volume preserved, resumable) and it is the guard against ~$25/hr
  idle burn on a wide pod. Surfaced to the user as an open decision.
- **SLURM `scancel` is NOT gated.** The fellows QoS ladder and the lane
  failover cancel OUR OWN queued jobs (never a teammate's). Surfaced to the
  user as an open decision.
